Ah - you mean the terminal emulator window on a Mac. That, along with the rest of the MacOS, is based on various open-source software projects: Mach, FreeBSD, GNU stuff released under GPLv2 (early version of the Gnu Public License which allowed the sort of commercial reuse that Apple is doing), and many smaller ones. There’s no Linux software there, although the functions and features so similar that a user can do many things the same way at a Mac or a Linux terminal emulator window. But once you get down into the source code and start poking around inside the operating system it becomes clear that they’re completely different OSes; the similarity comes from the many open-source utilities (including the shells that implement the command-line processing in the terminal window) that have been ported to the Mac and to Linux.
